simulator.title: See Sarajevo through different eyes.
simulator.intro: Choose a condition and drag the divider across the photo to compare clear vision with an approximate simulation.
simulator.sliderLabel: Comparison divider. Use the left and right arrow keys.
simulator.clearDesc: A sharp image at every distance, with full contrast and colour.
simulator.myopiaDesc: Near objects are sharp while distant ones blur — mountains and buildings far away lose detail.
simulator.hyperopiaDesc: Effort to focus, especially up close — the foreground is softer than the background.
simulator.astigmatismDesc: The image is stretched in one direction, with doubled outlines and shadows.
simulator.cataractDesc: A cloudy, yellowed view with reduced contrast and glare around light.
simulator.disclaimer: Illustrative only. The simulation does not represent an individual diagnosis or treatment outcome. An eye examination is needed to assess your vision.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of the eye, step by step.
anatomy.intro: Select a part of the eye to learn what it does and which of its conditions the clinic treats.
anatomy.note: Simplified educational cross-section of the eye. The illustration is not to scale and requires medical review before production.
anatomy.corneaText: The clear front “window” of the eye that bends light and provides most of the eye’s focusing power. Its shape determines your prescription — which is why it is reshaped in laser vision correction.
anatomy.lensText: The elastic lens behind the iris fine-tunes focus at different distances. With age it loses elasticity (presbyopia) or becomes cloudy (cataract).
anatomy.retinaText: A thin layer of nerve cells on the back wall of the eye that turns light into signals. Its centre — the macula — lets you read and recognise faces.
anatomy.irisText: The coloured part of the eye. Its muscles change the size of the pupil to control how much light enters.
anatomy.nerveText: Carries signals from the retina to the brain. Glaucoma gradually damages the optic nerve, often without any symptoms.

journey.title: With you every step of the way.
journey.intro: Every treatment plan is individual. This is how the path from first contact to follow-up most often looks.
journey.s1t: Call us or send a request online. The clinic team will contact you to confirm a time and explain how to prepare.
journey.s2t: The exam covers visual acuity, eye pressure and the whole eye, with imaging such as OCT or corneal topography where needed.
journey.s3t: Your doctor explains the findings and options — from glasses and medication to procedures — and answers your questions.
journey.s4t: Follow-up visits monitor your recovery. How often depends on the treatment and is set by your doctor.
journey.note: Steps are illustrative — the course of treatment varies with each diagnosis.

pages.aboutIntro: In Sarajevo since 2011 — part of the region’s largest group of eye clinics and a teaching department of the University of Sarajevo.
pages.aboutMeta: History, mission and values of Svjetlost Special Hospital for Ophthalmology, Sarajevo.
pages.missionText: To establish and develop a quality system that delivers excellent healthcare with continuous improvement across every department of the hospital.
pages.visionText: To be a healthcare institution recognised for the quality of its services, with the patient and their family at the centre of care.
pages.universityText: Svjetlost has become the Department of Ophthalmology of the University of Sarajevo, confirming its role in educating future specialists.
pages.dayHospitalText: Most eye operations are performed as day surgery — patients go home the same day.
pages.educationText: Each year the clinic hires young doctors who can specialise in ophthalmology, with visits to international congresses and leading centres.
pages.facilitiesText: Two operating theatres, six consulting rooms, a diagnostic centre, a pre-operative preparation room and sterilisation — designed after centres of medical excellence worldwide.
pages.awardsNote: Awards received by the Svjetlost group, according to the official website.
pages.networkText: Sarajevo is part of a regional network headquartered in Zagreb. Some procedures — such as corneal transplants or squint surgery — are performed in Zagreb.
